title: Make a Square with the Same Color
summary: Given a 3x3 grid where each cell is either 'B' (black) or 'W' (white), your task is to check if it is possible to change the color of at most one cell so that there exists a 2x2 square with all cells of the same color.
statement: Given a 3x3 grid where each cell is either 'B' (black) or 'W' (white), your task is to check if it is possible to change the color of at most one cell so that there exists a 2x2 square with all cells of the same color. Return true if such a change can create a 2x2 square of the same color, otherwise return false.
constraints: The grid is exactly three by three and every cell is B or W.
You may recolor at most one cell.
Return whether some two-by-two subgrid can be made a single color.
hints: A two-by-two block has four cells.
With at most one recoloring it can be uniform exactly when one color occupies at least three cells.
Count black cells in each of the four blocks; every count except two meets that condition.
Checking all block origins exhausts the possible target squares.
editorial: Checking all block origins exhausts the possible target squares.

tests.explanation: The lower-right two-by-two block contains three W cells and can be completed with one change.
Every two-by-two block is evenly split, so one recoloring cannot make it uniform.
